messages.subject: consultation about methylKit
parts:
Dear Pro., I have 2 questios. 1) when I use methylKit to analysis my rice bs-seq data, I filtered the low coverage C loci before read-in the txt file, and also sorted by chromosome and position, so the read-in files have different rows. but the output results have the same rows. Do the input files must have the same rows? 

2) There are CHH, CHG and CG in plants genome, so I deal with my data three times using the myobj parameter context = CHH, CHG and CG , respectively. I will combine the above three results and sort before to caculate DMR with the eDMR, yes or no?

Thank you very much.

On Nov 19, 2013, at 8:50 AM, 王西亮 wrote:

Dear Pro., I have 2 questios. 1) when I use methylKit to analysis my rice bs-seq data, I filtered the low coverage C loci before read-in the txt file, and also sorted by chromosome and position, so the read-in files have different rows. but the output results have the same rows. Do the input files must have the same rows?

The input files does not have to have the same rows. The unite function will handle that. Also, with the argument "min.per.group" you can specify "minimum number of samples per replicate needed to cover a region/base."

2) There are CHH, CHG and CG in plants genome, so I deal with my data three times using the myobj parameter context = CHH, CHG and CG , respectively. I will combine the above three results and sort before to caculate DMR with the eDMR, yes or no?

This depends on how you wanna treat the three different types of methylations. 
If you want to have a separate list of DMRs for CHH, CHG and CG, then call eDMR for each of the methDiff to get DMR results.
If you want to treat them as the same or similar function (I am not sure if this is true for rice), then you can combine all of them together to call eDMR.

Thank you very much.  


--

GOOD LUCK

Xiliang Wang
